high.title: Petrobras (PETR4): Oil Production in Brazil Advances 16.3% in Q1 2026; Exports Surge 61%
high.summary: Petrobras (PETR4) reported strong Q1 2026 results with average production reaching 3.197 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (boed), a 16.4% increase year-over-year. Oil production specifically jumped 16.3% to 2.583 million bpd, while oil exports surged 61.2% to 888,000 bpd. The production gains were primarily driven by ramp-up activities at several FPSOs including P-78 at Búzios field, Alexandre de Gusmão at Mero field, and Anna Nery and Anita Garibaldi at Marlim and Voador fields. Natural gas production also increased 16.5% to 613,000 boed. This robust operational performance is highly bullish for PETR4 shares and should support dividend expectations. The massive export increase (61%) is particularly positive for Brazil's trade balance and could provide modest BRL support. For equity investors, these results suggest strong cash flow generation and potential for higher shareholder returns. The production growth trajectory indicates Petrobras is successfully executing its deepwater expansion strategy in the pre-salt basins.

medium.title: Tokyo and Sydney Stock Exchanges Close Higher After Records in NY
medium.summary: Asian markets followed Wall Street's record highs with Tokyo's Nikkei rising 0.38% to 59,513.12 points and Sydney's S&P/ASX 200 advancing 0.74% to 8,729.80 points. The positive sentiment was driven by strong tech earnings from Alphabet and Qualcomm amid AI enthusiasm. However, risk appetite remained limited due to ongoing US-Iran tensions. This global risk-on sentiment could provide supportive flows for Brazilian equities if sustained.

medium.title: Gold Closes Higher with Uncertainties About US-Iran Negotiations Resumption
medium.summary: Gold futures closed 0.32% higher at $4,644.50 per troy ounce as investors weighed Iranian signals about resuming negotiations with the US. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated Tehran remains open to diplomacy if Washington changes its "expansionist posture." The continued geopolitical uncertainty supports safe-haven demand for gold, which could limit risk appetite for emerging market assets including Brazilian equities and potentially strengthen demand for Brazilian government bonds as investors seek yield with some safety.

medium.title: Trump Says He's Not Satisfied with Iran: 'We'll See What Happens with Negotiations'
medium.summary: President Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's fragmented leadership, stating negotiations have stalled after progress was made earlier. He noted that while all Iranian factions want a deal, they have conflicting demands that complicate reaching consensus. This ongoing uncertainty maintains geopolitical risk premiums in global markets, which could continue to support oil prices (beneficial for Petrobras) while potentially limiting risk appetite for emerging market assets including BRL and Brazilian equities.
